body.statement: Using the handle in \(\text{def:k-frontier-handle}\), determine whether \(\textsc{K-Fiber}\) on \(\mathfrak M_{p,K}^{\mathrm{forest}}\) has an \(f(K)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) decision-and-witness algorithm. If it does not, establish faithful rational W[1]- or W[2]-hardness with transformed budget linear in the source parameter and derive the corresponding ETH exclusion of \(f(K)N^{o(K)}\) time. Every negative-branch gadget must use the piecewise realization of \(\text{thm:rational-tree-realization}\) and independently verify the arbitrary-root SEM covariance identity, both directed residuals on each edge, positive definiteness, nonzero-edge faithfulness, rationality, polynomial bit length, every internal root, and every auxiliary label. The resolution must remain valid on the twin-star family.
body.justification: This is the answer-open theorem-level kernel: it classifies whether latent equality information can be exploited without enumerating \(N^{K}\) dictionaries.
body.gap: WuDrton2023 and PetersBuhlmann2014 settle supplied partitions and \(K=1\), while FellowsGuoKanj2010 settles unrestricted label systems; neither determines the Gaussian-realizable latent-\(K\) frontier.
body.consumer: The classification tells SEMgraph whether an exact latent-\(K\) bottom-up mode can scale with the number of variance groups or must expose a hardness warning.

obligation.what_is_open: For unbounded component size, determine whether root-locus geometry supports an \(f(K)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) decision-and-witness algorithm, or construct a faithful rational W[1]- or W[2]-hardness reduction with budget linear in the source parameter and the corresponding ETH lower bound.
obligation.obstruction: The half-tree locus restrictions make realizable root-signature systems substantially narrower than arbitrary minimum-label choice systems. No selector-and-compatibility construction has been certified against every internal root, the rational-square edge constraints, and unintended auxiliary labels; conversely, the locus characterization alone does not bound a dictionary certificate solely as a function of \(K\).
obligation.attempted: The available branching invariant was pushed to the exact \(d^K\) algorithm, and the inverse covariance calculation was completed so that any future gadget can be checked without an unproved realization step. Common-center star selectors fail because a cheap common root satisfies all choices, while varying centers create complementary residual labels whose budget is not linear.
obligation.partial_result: The closed results establish an exact dictionary-feasibility test through \(R_j(D)\), an explicit decision-and-witness algorithm with running time \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\), and a complete inverse-realization criterion for any proposed rational tree gadget.  Thus fixed-parameter tractability is proved whenever component size \(d\) is bounded as a function of \(K\).  What remains unresolved is whether the root-locus geometry yields an \(f(K)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) algorithm for unbounded \(d\), or instead admits a faithful rational parameterized-hard family with transformed budget linear in the source parameter.
